targets.authors: Gailliot, M. T., Baumeister, R. F., DeWall, C. N., Maner, J. K., Plant, E. A., Tice, D. M., et al.
targets.title: Self-control relies on glucose as a limited energy source. Willpower is more than a metaphor.
targets.evidence_quote: The present study was designed to comply with the widespread call for replications by applying study protocols reported to results in substantial effects of sugar consumption (Gailliot et al., 2007; Wang & Dvorak, 2010) and sugar sensing (Hagger & Chatzisarantis, 2012; Molden et al., 2012) on ego depletion. The resulting observation that these procedures did not lead to the detection of the originally reported effects underscores the relevance of independent replications.
targets.outcome_quote: Two experimental designs involving highly reliable, prototypical self-control tasks and yielding more than sufﬁcient power failed to replicate the previously reported effects of glucose ingestion (Gailliot et al., 2007; Hagger et al., 2010) and glucose sensing (Hagger & Chatzisarantis, 2012; Molden et al., 2012).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report failure to replicate this published glucose effect. Limitations are discussed, but their substantive overall judgment remains failure, rather than an inability to adjudicate.

targets.authors: Wang, X. T., & Dvorak, R. D.
targets.title: Sweet future ﬂuctuating blood glucose levels affect future discounting.
targets.evidence_quote: Experiment 1 was designed to replicate the counteracting effect of sugar consumption on ego depletion (Gailliot et al., 2007; Hagger et al., 2010). Following the protocol of Wang and Dvorak (2010), participants’ delay-discounting rates were assessed prior and after the consumption of a sweet drink containing either sugar or artiﬁcial sweetener.
targets.outcome_quote:
